findings.claim: The `impl._bytes ?? impl._buffer` fallback silently degrades to `undefined` when neither internal field exists (e.g. a future jsdom rename), producing a Blob whose content is the literal string "undefined" instead of failing loudly.
findings.rationale: `new NodeBlob_([undefined])` does not throw — Node's Blob constructor stringifies non-BufferSource parts, so the result is a 9-byte blob containing "undefined". Because the code now explicitly tolerates one of the two names being missing, a third rename would no longer produce a clear `TypeError` (as the old `undefined._buffer` access did for a missing impl); it would instead yield silently corrupted upload/fetch bodies that are very hard to trace. A guard such as `const bytes = impl?._bytes ?? impl?._buffer; if (bytes == null) throw new Error('Unsupported jsdom Blob internals')` would keep the failure explicit. High confidence on the mechanics; medium on whether the project considers this worth handling.

findings.claim: `impl` is still dereferenced without a null check, so a Blob not backed by a jsdom impl (cross-realm or subclassed Blob) throws a raw `TypeError` from inside the compat helper.
findings.rationale: `(blob as any)[implSymbol]` is `undefined` for any Blob that did not come from this jsdom window; `impl._bytes` then throws "Cannot read properties of undefined". This is pre-existing behavior, but the change touched exactly this expression and introduced an `impl` local, so it is a cheap place to add `impl?.` plus a descriptive error. Low-to-medium confidence that such blobs actually reach this helper.

findings.claim: Assumes jsdom 28's `_bytes` is a BufferSource with the same semantics as the old `_buffer`; if it is a `Uint8Array` view into a larger pooled ArrayBuffer, correctness depends on Node's Blob honoring byteOffset/byteLength.
findings.rationale: Node's Blob constructor does respect the view's byteOffset/byteLength, so this is most likely fine, but the rename from `_buffer` (Node Buffer) to `_bytes` (likely Uint8Array) is a type change, not just a name change — worth confirming against the jsdom 28 implementation, and worth a test asserting blob byte equality for a non-trivial payload. Low confidence that this is an actual bug.
